highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: US Labor Market Snapshot — October 2026
highlights.summary: Monthly snapshot of US job postings, wages, unemployment, and openings as of October 2026, providing the most current real-time labor demand indicators available for tracking AI-era hiring trends.

highlights.title: The hidden costs of technological change: investigating pathways through which highly automatable jobs undermine workers' health in Germany
highlights.summary: Peer-reviewed study identifying causal pathways by which high automation-exposure jobs harm worker well-being in Germany, quantifying displacement-adjacent stress and skills-pressure mechanisms relevant to displacement risk modeling.

highlights.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy and Wage Gaps: Evidence from China
highlights.summary: Using panel data for 280 Chinese cities from 2011–2023, exploits AI pilot zone designations as a natural experiment to estimate AI policy's effect on urban wage gaps, providing quasi-experimental wage evidence mappable to skill-premium dynamics.

highlights.title: When AI Enters the Workplace, Who Faces Greater Risk? A Gendered Analysis
highlights.summary: AAAI/AIES peer-reviewed paper quantifying differential AI displacement risk by gender using occupational exposure assessments, finding women face structurally higher risk due to concentration in AI-vulnerable roles.

highlights.title: The Economic Implications of Artificial Intelligence for Employment and Labour Productivity: A Descriptive Evidence Synthesis (2020–2025)
highlights.summary: Synthesizes enterprise AI-adoption statistics, occupational-exposure assessments, and empirical workplace studies from 2020–2025 to distinguish technological augmentation from substitution effects on employment and productivity.

highlights.title: AI-driven 'new migrants': skill-spatial mismatch and out-migration intention
highlights.summary: Using China Migrant Population Dynamic Monitoring Survey and patent data across 250 cities (2014–2018), quantifies how AI-induced skill-spatial mismatch drives internal out-migration, linking automation exposure to geographic labor reallocation.

highlights.title: When Do AI Gains Become Broadly Shareable? A Policy Threshold for AI-Driven Automation
highlights.summary: Extends a standard task-automation growth model with an AI capability parameter to derive policy thresholds at which automation productivity gains become broadly distributable, providing a quantitative framework for wage-impact timing.

highlights.title: Supporting or Replacing Students' Reasoning? Cognitive Offloading in AI-Assisted Proof Learning
highlights.summary: RCT with 153 undergraduates using staggered AI chatbot access finds measurable differences in learning outcomes between early- and late-access groups, providing causal evidence on AI's role in education-sector skill formation.

highlights.title: Artificial Intelligence, Automation, and the Sustainability of Social Security Systems: The Technological Unemployment Premium Proposal
highlights.summary: Qualitative synthesis examining how AI-driven labor displacement threatens contribution-based social security funding, proposing a 'technological unemployment premium' levy on automation beneficiaries as a fiscal stabilizer.

highlights.title: WORKFORCE TRANSFORMATION IN MANUFACTURING INDUSTRIES: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AUTOMATION, RESKILLING, UPSKILLING AND SOFT SKILLS
highlights.summary: Empirical study of AI and robotics adoption in manufacturing industries assessing displacement, reskilling demand, and skill-mix shifts, with quantitative evidence on workforce capability gaps in physical automation contexts.
